title: Young minds in distress: Exploring the global rise in youth mental health diagnoses
title_zh: 青少年心理健康诊断的全球上升：探索青少年心理健康诊断的全球增长
abstract: Adolescence represents a critical neurobiological period marked by a developmental “mismatch” between early-maturing limbic systems and the later-maturing prefrontal cortex, conferring heightened vulnerability to the onset of psychiatric disorders. This review synthesizes global epidemiological trends, differentiates true increases in morbidity from diagnostic inflation, and integrates evidence-based intervention strategies. In high-income countries, youth depression, suicide mortality, and self-harm have risen substantially, supported by objective indicators of illness severity that extend beyond changes in diagnostic practices. Key environmental drivers include pervasive digital engagement, cyberbullying, sleep disruption, and academic pressure, with sleep disturbances emerging as a central transdiagnostic risk factor. The COVID-19 pandemic accelerated these pre-existing trajectories of mental health deterioration, with particularly marked effects on eating-disorder incidence and social-emotional development. To address these challenges, we suggest a three-tiered intervention framework. Universal approaches should emphasize regulation of digital environments, implementation of Social-Emotional Learning, and institutional support for regular physical activity. Selective interventions should target high-risk youth by proactively monitoring sleep health and mitigating achievement-related stress in academically competitive settings. Indicated care requires integrated delivery of evidence-based psychotherapies alongside structured return-to-learn protocols following psychiatric hospitalization. Ultimately, translating epidemiological risk into effective prevention demands a shift from reactive, diagnosis-centered models to proactive frameworks that prioritize early risk reduction and the reinforcement of protective factors. By fostering environments that promote circadian stability, physical activity, emotional regulation, and peer connectedness, youth mental health can be strengthened as a foundation for societal well-being, resilience, and adaptive functioning in an increasingly complex world.
abstract_zh: 青春期是一个关键的神经生物学时期，其特征是早熟的边缘系统与后成熟的前额叶皮层之间发育性“错位”，这使其对精神疾病的发病具有高度脆弱性。本综述综合了全球流行病学趋势，区分了真实的病率增加与诊断膨胀，并整合了基于证据的干预策略。在高收入国家，青少年抑郁、自杀死亡率和自伤行为显著增加，这得到了超越诊断惯变化的疾病严重程度客观指标的支持。关键的环境驱动因素包括普遍的数字参与、网络欺凌、睡眠中断和学业压力，其中睡眠障碍被确定为一个贯穿各类精神疾病的核心危险因素。COVID-19大流行加速了既有的心理健康恶化趋势，特别是在饮食障碍发病率和社交情感发展方面产生了显著影响。为了应对这些挑战，我们提出了一个三层次的干预框架。普遍性方法应侧重于数字环境的监管、社会情感学习的实施以及机构对规律体育活动的支持。选择性干预应针对高危青少年，通过主动监测睡眠健康并在学术竞争激烈的环境中缓解成就相关压力。指示性护理需要在证据-based 心理治疗的综合交付和精神住院后的结构化“归校”协议之间进行整合。最终，将流行病学风险转化为有效预防，要求从以诊断为中心的反应模式转向优先考虑早期风险降低和保护因素强化的主动框架。通过促进昼夜节律稳定、体育活动、情绪调节和同伴联结的环境，青少年心理健康可以作为社会福祉、韧性和日益复杂世界中适应功能的基础得到加强。
